answer: An agent marketplace requires each bidding identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before submitting offers. Whether agents sell sable fabric, violet dye, or spiral notebooks, the same rule applies. Creating 10,000 fake bidders therefore ties up $1 million for a month. New names remain cheap, but each usable identity consumes scarce capital, making a swarm costly to maintain even if its bids never win.
